name: רְחַבְיָהוּ
summary: Rehabiah, the only son of Eliezer son of Moses, a Levite whose sons “were very many”, so that his house became one of the courses of Levites under David, headed by Isshiah, and his descendant Shelomoth was over the treasuries of the dedicated things (1Ch 23:17; 24:21; 26:25–26). The name is the verb רָחַב “make wide” with יָהּ: “Yahweh has made wide”, as Isaac said at Rehoboth, “now Yahweh has made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land” (Gen 26:22). Scripture does not explain it, but it records that his sons were many.

evidence.note: “The sons of Eliezer: רְחַבְיָה the head; Eliezer had no other sons, but the sons of Rehabiah רָבוּ לְמָעְלָה”: were very many.
“Of Rehabiah: of the sons of Rehabiah, Isshiah the head.”
“Rehabiah his son”, in the line to Shelomoth over the treasuries.
The verb with Yahweh as subject: “now Yahweh הִרְחִיב לָנוּ, and we shall be fruitful in the land.”

note: Spelled רְחַבְיָה (1Ch 23:17, twice) and רְחַבְיָהוּ (1Ch 24:21; 26:25). The reading “Yahweh has made wide” takes the first part as the verb (perfect) with the divine name as subject; the hiphil sense “make room” fits it, but the form is not explained in scripture.
